Water requirements for process, cooling and blow-down would be highly dependent on the type of facility, capacity and type of cooling. Water consumption could be as much as 16,000 acre-feet per year for gasification. Presumably, this water would come from Yellowtail Dam or the Yellowstone River; Westmoreland Resources currently holds a contract for 30,000 acre feet annually from Yellowtail Dam for industrial use, which would be more than sufficient to meet estimated water requirements.
Use of approximately 16,000 acre feet annually would preempt for other uses this amount of water for the life of the project. Since water is a critical resource of limited supply in this area, its equitable and effective utilization is a major concern among the region's residents. Allocations of natural water flows in this river are presented in Appendix M of the U.S. Bureau of Indian Affairs draft programmatic environmental statement titled, "Projected Coal Development Crow Indian Reservation" (1975). In this same report, results are presented (p. 206-209) for the annual water year depletion studies of streamflow in the Bighorn River, conducted by the Bureau of Reclamation.
